description: A conceptual comparison: an imagined mound made from as many sand grains as molecules in a cubic centimetre of air could cover a large factory. This is not a measured pile, coordinate diagram or literal construction proposal.

authoritativeText.text: 由于分子很小，所以每个物体中所包含的分子数都很大。例如，一滴水内所包含的分子数是居住在地球上的人口数的几百亿倍。1 厘米$^3$ 空气中所包含的分子数是如此之大，以致若把相同数目的细沙粒堆积起来就会成为一座小山，这座山可以覆盖住一个大工厂（图 14）。

inventory.description: Original pixels show a broad cone of many fine stippled grains behind the factory, extending beyond its skyline and both sides. It is one imagined pile, with no labelled dimensions or measurable data. Modern natural colors and grain shading are illustration changes, not geological information.

A single industrial complex crosses the foreground at the pile's foot: connected low buildings, taller sections, several chimneys and a little exhaust. The mound is conspicuously taller and wider. No people, vehicles, flags, symbols, scale or labels are printed. Colors and clean building details are modern neutral regularization, not additional scientific conditions.
